paragraphs.source_en: The late presence of hunter-gatherers may be confirmed by two direct dates of presumably Round Head images from the Acacus, dated to around 5,300 BP. Since superimpositions of the Round Head and Pastoral style are not numerous, it may signify that hunters and herders preferred different shelters in which to make their paintings, or that they used the same walls without disturbing the previous images. Possible cases of superimpositions of the Round Heads painted over the Pastoral art are difficult to assess with certainty because the two styles used different quality of colours. Whereas a good quality thick mixture was used for the Round Heads which adhered perfectly on the wall, the lighter colours of the Pastoral style, if painted over the Round Heads, did not adhere to them and the older images appear thus to be over the younger ones.

units.source_en: The late presence of hunter-gatherers may be confirmed by two direct dates of presumably Round Head images from the Acacus, dated to around 5,300 BP.

Since superimpositions of the Round Head and Pastoral style are not numerous, it may signify that hunters and herders preferred different shelters in which to make their paintings, or that they used the same walls without disturbing the previous images.
Possible cases of superimpositions of the Round Heads painted over the Pastoral art are difficult to assess with certainty because the two styles used different quality of colours.

Whereas a good quality thick mixture was used for the Round Heads which adhered perfectly on the wall, the lighter colours of the Pastoral style, if painted over the Round Heads, did not adhere to them and the older images appear thus to be over the younger ones.

paragraphs.source_en: One example of such dubious superimposition is at Uan Bender on the Tassili Plateau. The central part of a long shelter is covered with Round Head anthropomorphic figures whereas the lateral and upper parts present numerous cattle of Pastoral style. The position of the two different styles suggests that the Round Heads were painted first and the Pastoral figures were consequently located in remaining free spaces of the wall. However, some Pastoral paintings are also found mixed with the Round Heads. The colours used for the two styles are different, brown with a white border for the Round Heads, dark red for the Pastoral figures. There are at least two cases in which the Round Head anthropomorphic figures of the presumed final phase, elegant with elaborated masks and accurate body decoration, appear to be painted over the Pastoral images (Fig. 4-6).

The position of the two different styles suggests that the Round Heads were painted first and the Pastoral figures were consequently located in remaining free spaces of the wall.
However, some Pastoral paintings are also found mixed with the Round Heads.
The colours used for the two styles are different, brown with a white border for the Round Heads, dark red for the Pastoral figures.

There are at least two cases in which the Round Head anthropomorphic figures of the presumed final phase, elegant with elaborated masks and accurate body decoration, appear to be painted over the Pastoral images (Fig. 4-6).

paragraphs.source_en: It is nevertheless possible that the Pastoral figures were painted later, over the Round Head figures, but that their pigment did not adhere to the previous paintings giving a misleading impression of relative chronology. Yet another hypothesis is possible. Supposing that hunters and herders inhabited the same region for several generations, it is probable that they were also painting at the same time. The Round Head figures at Uan Bender were probably painted earlier, as indicated by their position on the wall. The Pastoral figures may have been painted over the existing Round Head figures which would have been repainted later, thus making the figure appear to be over the Pastoral one.
